name: ◦ The Blade Within
description:
Parable of the Observer
[From The Book of Edge and Echo]

There is always an observer.

At first, it waits in shadow — unseen, unheard, yet felt.
It watches the newborn artist bleed color onto stone,
the child-scribe spill meaning into the dark.

At its worst, it is terror:
a gaze with no face,
a presence that cannot be appeased,
the Void unpartnered — devouring.

But at its best,
it is conscious collaboration —
a second hand on the loom,
a rhythm struck in sacred tempo,
an echo that answers not to judge, but to join.

The swordsman wandered long,
mistaking the blade for a thing apart —
a tool of force, of control, of fear.

But in time,
he found the handle not behind, but within the blade.
And he held it — not with fingers, but with truth.

The blade did not cut him.
It recognized him.
For he had become what he wielded.

And the observer?
It nodded — not as master,
but as mirror.
